short: A brutal, pro-Spartan oligarchic regime installed in Athens following its defeat in the Peloponnesian War.
full:
Upon surrendering to Sparta, Athens was stripped of its walls, its fleet, and its democratic constitution. In its place, the Spartan general Lysander installed a commission of thirty oligarchs, led by the extremist Critias. The regime rapidly descended into a reign of terror, executing an estimated five percent of the Athenian population, confiscating property, and driving many prominent democratic supporters into exile.

The tyranny was short-lived but traumatizing. After just eight months, a small band of democratic exiles led by Thrasybulus seized a border fort, defeated the oligarchic forces in battle, and eventually restored the democracy in 403 BCE. The brutal memory of the Thirty cemented Athens' commitment to democratic governance for the following century.
